extracted.intended_audience: parties and practitioners appearing before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (owners, requesters, respondents, and their counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content rules governing briefs, answers, rebuttals, hearings, motions, and filings in PTAB appeals and contested cases, including formatting, service, timing, and remedy options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and one-time filing of respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent(s) in an appeal may once, within the time limit for filing set forth in § 41.66, file a respondent brief and serve the brief on all parties in accordance with § 1.903 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent may file only one respondent brief and must do so within the deadline prescribed by § 41.66; service must comply with service rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and fee for respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must be signed by the party, or the party’s duly authorized attorney or agent, and must be accompanied by the requisite fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsigned briefs or briefs missing the required fee are non-compliant and subject to notification for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent brief shall be limited to issues raised in the appellant brief to which the respondent brief is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent cannot raise new issues beyond those presented by the appellant brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester cannot address others' briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester’s respondent brief may not address any brief of any other requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each requester is limited to responding to the appellant's brief (or owner) and may not respond to other requesters' briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief required content and order
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent brief shall contain the following items under appropriate headings and in the order here indicated, and may include an appendix containing only those portions of the record on which reliance has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to include required headings/items in order may trigger a notice to amend; appendices limited to relied-upon record portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Real Party in Interest. A statement identifying by name the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must expressly identify all real parties in interest by name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of related appeals, interferences, and trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Related Appeals, Interferences, and trials. A statement identifying by application, patent, appeal, interference, or trial number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences or judicial proceedings known to respondent... which may be related to, directly affect or be directly affected by or have a bearing on the Board’s decision in the pending appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of any decisions rendered in identified proceedings must be included in an appendix as required by paragraph (b)(1)(ix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims: acceptance or dispute with particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Status of claims. A statement accepting or disputing appellant’s statement of the status of claims. If appellant’s statement of the status of claims is disputed, the errors in appellant’s statement must be specified with particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simply denying appellant's status is insufficient—must specify precise errors (with record citations as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments: acceptance or dispute with particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Status of amendments. A statement accepting or disputing appellant’s statement of the status of amendments. If appellant’s statement of the status of amendments is disputed, the errors in appellant’s statement must be specified with particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must specifically identify and explain any alleged errors in appellant's characterization of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter: acceptance or dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of claimed subject matter. A statement accepting or disputing appellant’s summary of the subject matter defined in each of the independent claims involved in the appeal. If appellant’s summary of the subject matter is disputed, the errors in appellant’s summary must be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disputes to appellant's claim summaries must be particularized; include precise points of contention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues to be reviewed on appeal: accept/dispute and counter-statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues to be reviewed on appeal. A statement accepting or disputing appellant’s statement of the issues presented for review. If appellant’s statement of the issues presented for review is disputed, the errors in appellant’s statement must be specified. A counter statement of the issues for review may be made. No new ground of rejection can be proposed by a requester respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may present counter-statements of issues but may not assert new grounds of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument content and structure in respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument. A statement accepting or disputing the contentions of appellant with each of the issues presented by the appellant for review. If a contention of the appellant is disputed, the errors in appellant’s argument must be specified, stating the basis therefor, with citations of the statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the record relied on. Each issue must be treated under a separate heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments must be organized under separate headings per issue, specify errors with legal citations and record references; counter-stated issues must also be separately headed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix and limitation to entered evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence appendix. An appendix containing copies of any evidence submitted pursuant to §§ 1.130, 1.131, or 1.132 of this title or of any other evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon by respondent in the appeal, along with a statement setting forth where in the record that evidence was entered in the record by the examiner. Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted in the respondent’s brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only evidence that has been entered by the examiner or submitted under the specified rules may be relied on and appended; must state where evidence appears in the record; unentered evidence cannot be referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related proceedings appendix (decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related proceedings appendix. An appendix containing copies of decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified pursuant to paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include copies of any judicial or Board decisions from proceedings identified as related.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service for respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate of service. A certification that a copy of the respondent brief has been served in its entirety on all other parties to the reexamination proceeding. The names and addresses of the parties served must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate must list names and addresses of all served parties and state the manner/date of service (see § 41.106(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new or non‑admitted amendments/evidence in respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new grounds, amendments, affidavits or evidence not previously admitted must be filed through the appropriate amendment/evidence procedures (e.g., § 1.116 or § 41.63), not in the respondent brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance notice and limited time to amend respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent brief is filed which does not comply with all the requirements of paragraph (a) and paragraph (b) of this section, respondent will be notified of the reasons for non-compliance and given a non-extendable time period within which to file an amended brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file an amended brief that overcomes stated deficiencies will result in the brief not being considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's answer may explain but may not introduce new rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer including such explanation of the invention claimed and of the references relied upon, the grounds of rejection, and the reasons for patentability. An examiner’s answer may not include a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners can clarify and explain positions but cannot assert new grounds of rejection in the answer; new grounds must be made in an Office action reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner cannot make new determination to not adopt proposed rejection in answer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s answer may not include a new determination not to make a proposed rejection of a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such determinations must be made in an Office action reopening prosecution, not in the examiner’s answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief timing and one-time filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month of the examiner’s answer, any appellant may once file a rebuttal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuttal briefs are limited to a single filing by an appellant and must be timely (one month).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief limitations on topics and parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief of a requester may not be directed to the respondent brief of any other requester. The rebuttal brief of the owner may be directed to the examiner’s answer and/or any respondent brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester rebuttals must be confined; owner may respond to examiner and respondent briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new grounds or new evidence in rebuttal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: No new ground of rejection can be proposed by a requester. The rebuttal brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or an affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuttals cannot introduce new rejections or new/unadmitted evidence or amendments; see § 1.116 and § 41.63 for post-appeal evidence/amendment handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service for rebuttal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief must include a certification that a copy of the rebuttal brief has been served in its entirety on all other parties to the proceeding. The names and addresses of the parties served must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with other filings, a certificate of service is mandatory and must identify parties and addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance procedure for rebuttal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rebuttal brief is timely filed but does not comply with all the requirements of paragraphs (a) through (d), appellant will be notified of the reasons for non-compliance and provided with a non-extendable period of one month within which to file an amended rebuttal brief. Failure to timely correct results in the rebuttal brief not being considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict one-month cure period; failure to cure means brief (and any amended brief) not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to request an oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only in those circumstances in which an appellant or a respondent considers such a hearing necessary or desirable for a proper presentation of the appeal. An appeal decided on the briefs without an oral hearing will receive the same consideration by the Board as an appeal decided after an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral hearings are discretionary—request only when needed; absence of a hearing does not diminish consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and fee for requesting oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellant or a respondent desires an oral hearing, he or she must file, as a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING,' a written request for such hearing accompanied by the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(3) within two months after the date of the examiner’s answer. The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be separate, captioned correctly, include the fee, and meet the non-extendable two-month deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service certification for oral hearing request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a certification that a copy of the request has been served in its entirety on all other parties to the proceeding. The names and addresses of the parties served must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same service/certificate requirements apply to hearing requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of no timely oral hearing request
rubrics_metrics.description: If no request and fee for oral hearing have been timely filed by appellant or respondent as required, the appeal will be assigned for consideration and decision on the briefs without an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely request and pay for a hearing means the appeal proceeds on the briefs only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing participation and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral hearing is held, an oral argument may be presented by, or on behalf of, the primary examiner if considered desirable. Oral argument will be limited to thirty minutes for each appellant or respondent who has requested an oral hearing, and twenty minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict time limits apply; Board sets order of arguments; no participation without request and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and argument at oral hearing limited to entered record
rubrics_metrics.description: At the oral hearing, each appellant and respondent may only rely on evidence that has been previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present argument that has been relied upon in the briefs except as permitted by paragraph (e)(2) (good-cause new argument based on recent decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New evidence is generally barred at oral hearing; new arguments only on good cause showing and limited to recent relevant decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decisions: affirm, reverse, remand and new ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may affirm or reverse each decision of the examiner on all issues raised on each appealed claim, or remand the reexamination proceeding. The reversal of the examiner’s determination not to make a rejection proposed by a third party requester constitutes a decision adverse to patentability and will be set forth as a new ground of rejection. The Board may include new grounds of rejection; such decisions are not final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Board states a new ground of rejection, special procedural options (reopen prosecution or rehearing) become available to the owner and the decision is not final for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner options after new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board makes a new ground of rejection, the owner, within one month from the date of the decision, must either (1) reopen prosecution by filing an amendment or new evidence relating to the claims so rejected, or (2) request rehearing addressing the new ground and stating with particularity points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner must act within one month to avoid termination of appeal as to the rejected claim; reopening requires amendment and/or new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester comments after owner response to new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Where owner has filed a response requesting reopening of prosecution, any requester, within one month of the date of service of the owner’s response, may once file comments on the response limited to issues raised by the Board’s opinion and the owner’s response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters who had not previously filed an appeal/cross-appeal and now seek to comment are subject to appeal and brief fees under § 41.20(b)(1) and (2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to examiner and binding effect of Board statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Following owner response and requester comments, the proceeding will be remanded to the examiner. The statement of the Board shall be binding upon the examiner unless an amendment or new evidence not previously of record is made which, in the opinion of the examiner, overcomes the new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must follow Board statement unless owner submits new matter that in examiner's view overcomes the new ground; examiner will then determine whether rejection is maintained or overcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments and replies after examiner determination on remand
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month of the examiner’s determination that the rejection is maintained or overcome, the owner or any requester may once submit comments in response to the examiner’s determination; within one month of service of comments, owner and any requesters may file a reply. No requester reply may address the comments of any other requester reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict one-time filing rights and one-month windows; fees may apply to requesters who had not previously appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration and incorporation of earlier decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission of any comments and replies, or after time has expired, the proceeding will be returned to the Board which shall reconsider the matter and issue a new decision. The new decision is deemed to incorporate the earlier decision, except for those portions specifically withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board's new decision builds on prior decision(s) except where portions are expressly withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time extensions limited and controlled
rubrics_metrics.description: The time period for owner action under paragraph (b) is subject to the extension provisions of § 1.956 when the owner is responding under paragraph (b)(1). The time period may not be extended when the owner is responding under paragraph (b)(2). Time periods in paragraphs (c) and (e) may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are tightly controlled; know which response scenarios permit extensions under § 1.956.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing: timing and particularity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file a request for rehearing of the decision within one month of the date of (various board decisions). The request for rehearing must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked in rendering the Board’s opinion. Arguments not raised in the briefs and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted except as allowed by good cause/new-ground exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing is narrowly circumscribed—must focus on specific alleged errors; do not introduce new arguments/evidence except per permitted exceptions (recent decisions or responding to a new ground).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing procedural limits and oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month of service of any request for rehearing, the owner and all requesters may once file comments in opposition limited to the issues raised in the request for rehearing. The decision on rehearing is generally final for judicial review except as noted; further rehearing of a new decision is possible within one month if Board indicates the opinion is effectively a new decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions to rehearing are limited in scope; rehearing timelines are not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of rehearing before judicial appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may not appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit until all parties’ rights to request rehearing have been exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must allow rehearing windows to lapse or be resolved before seeking judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contested-case notice of proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of a contested case will be sent to every party to the proceeding; the entry of the notice initiates the proceeding. If actual notice cannot be provided through the correspondence address of record, the Board may authorize other modes of notice (sending to another address associated with the party or publishing in the Official Gazette).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should ensure their correspondence addresses are accurate; Board has discretion to use alternative notice methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of examination before initiating contested case
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a contested case is initiated, except as the Board may otherwise authorize, examination or reexamination must be completed, and there must be at least one claim that (1) is patentable but for a judgment in the contested case, and (2) would be involved in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contested cases normally start only after examination is complete and at least one potentially patentable claim exists that would be affected by the contested case outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board jurisdiction and suspension of other proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board acquires jurisdiction over any involved file when the Board initiates a contested case. Other proceedings for the involved file within the Office are suspended except as the Board may order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a contested case is initiated, prosecution and other Office actions are generally suspended unless the Board orders otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to manage proceedings and waive rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may determine a proper course of conduct for any situation not specifically covered and may enter non-final orders to administer the proceeding. An administrative patent judge may waive or suspend in a proceeding the application of any rule in this subpart, subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board/administrative patent judges have procedural flexibility to manage cases and, in limited circumstances, waive or suspend certain rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default time rules and order-of-order-of-precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Times set in this subpart are defaults. In the event of a conflict between a time set by rule and a time set by order, the time set by order is controlling. Action due on a day other than a business day may be completed on the next business day unless the Board expressly states otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board orders can override default rule times; compute deadlines with business-day rules in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper format: paper size, color, single-sided requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper used for filings must be durable and white. A party must choose to file on either A4-sized paper or 8½ inch x 11 inch paper except for exhibits requiring larger size; a party may not switch between paper sizes in a single proceeding. Only one side of the paper may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent paper size and single-sided durable white paper required; exhibits that need larger sizes are excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font, ink, spacing, and margin requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Markings must be in black ink or otherwise provide an equivalently permanent, dark, high-contrast image. Printing quality must be equivalent to laser printer. Proportional fonts must be 12-point or larger; monospaced fonts must not contain more than 4 characters per centimeter. Double spacing must be used except in headings, tables of contents, tables of authorities, indices, signature blocks, and certificates of service. Block quotations may be single-spaced and must be indented. Margins must be at least 2.5 cm (1 inch) on all sides. Case names must be underlined or italicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow typographic standards strictly to avoid non-compliance; exceptions for headings/tables/quotations noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet and identification requirements for papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover sheet must include the caption the Board specifies for the proceeding, a header indicating the party and contact information for the party, and a title indicating the sequence and subject of the paper. If the Board specifies a color other than white for the cover sheet, the cover sheet must be that color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Board-specified caption and include clear contact info and a descriptive title (e.g., 'JONES MOTION 2, For benefit of an earlier application').

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical binding/holes for papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must have two 0.5 cm (¼ inch) holes with centers 1 cm (½ inch) from the top of the page and 7 cm (2¾ inch) apart, centered horizontally on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical filing layout requirement—ensure hole placement matches spec.

rubrics_metrics.name: No incorporation by reference; no combined papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments must not be incorporated by reference from one paper into another paper. Combined motions, oppositions, replies, or other combined papers are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each filing must be self-contained; do not rely on incorporation by reference across papers or combine different procedural papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper filed must be accompanied by a working copy marked 'APJ Copy'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an APJ Copy with every filing to facilitate the judges' review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by mail and other modes of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper filed using Priority Mail Express® will be deemed filed as of 'date accepted' on the mailing label; otherwise mail will be deemed filed as of the stamped date of receipt at the Board. The Board may authorize other modes of filing, including electronic filing and hand filing, and may set conditions for such modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Priority Mail Express® for earliest filing date certainty; follow Board authorizations for electronic or hand filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service methods and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed with the Board, if not previously served, must be served simultaneously on every opposing party except as the Board expressly directs. If a party is represented by counsel, service must be on counsel. Service must be by Priority Mail Express® or by means at least as fast and reliable; electronic service is not permitted without Board authorization. The date of service does not count in computing the time for responding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use permitted fast/reliable service methods; do not rely on electronic service unless authorized; track service dates (service date excluded from response deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service content and affidavit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers other than exhibits must include a certificate of service as a separate page at the end of each paper that must be served on an opposing party. Exhibits must be accompanied by a certificate of service, but a single certificate may accompany any group of exhibits submitted together. A certificate of service must state the date and manner of service, the name and address of every person served, and for exhibits filed as a group, the name and number of each exhibit served. A certificate made by a person other than a registered practitioner must be in the form of an affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure certificates of service are accurate and complete; non-practitioner certifiers must use affidavit form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead counsel identification and power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may be represented by counsel. The Board may require a party to appoint a lead counsel. If counsel is not of record in a party’s involved application or patent, then a power of attorney for that counsel for the party’s involved application or patent must be filed with the notice required in paragraph (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File notices identifying counsel and, if required, a power of attorney for counsel not already of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information filing within 14 days of initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days of the initiation of each contested case, each party must file a separate notice identifying its counsel, if any, and providing contact information for each counsel identified or, if the party has no counsel, then for the party. Contact information must include at minimum a mailing address, courier address, telephone number, facsimile number, and electronic mail address. A party must promptly notify the Board of any change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and complete contact information is mandatory; update promptly upon changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to and copies of Office records procedure and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request from a party for access to or copies of Office records directly related to a contested case must be filed with the Board and precisely identify the records; in the case of copies include the appropriate fee. Access and copies will ordinarily only be authorized for the application file for an involved patent, an involved application, and an application for which a party has been accorded benefit under subpart E. If a party does not receive a complete copy within 21 days of authorization, the party must promptly notify the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow request-and-fee procedure; expect authorization for limited categories of records; alert Board if copies are incomplete or missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing clean and annotated copies of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days of the initiation of the proceeding, each party must file a clean copy of its involved claims. Within 28 days, each party must file annotated copies where limitations are illustrated in drawings or biotechnology sequences, indicating in bold face between braces where each limitation is shown; for 35 U.S.C. 112(f) limitations, indicate spec portions describing structure/material/acts corresponding to each claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submit both clean and, when applicable, annotated claim copies; required annotations aid claim construction and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions: types, burden, and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions may be substantive (e.g., to redefine scope, change benefit, or for judgment), responsive (e.g., to amend/add claim), or miscellaneous. The party filing the motion has the burden of proof. Each motion must be filed as a separate paper and include: (i) a statement of the precise relief requested, (ii) a statement of material facts, and (iii) a full statement of the reasons for the relief requested, including detailed explanation of the significance of the evidence and the governing law, rules, and precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions must be separately captioned, factually precise, and legally detailed; include claim charts when comparing claims; Board may require additional showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of material facts format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each material fact shall be set forth as a separate numbered sentence with specific citations to the portions of the record that support the fact. The Board may require that the statement of material facts be submitted as a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numbered, discrete factual statements with record citations; failure to do so may be deemed admission of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim chart requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim charts must be used in support of any paper requiring the comparison of a claim to something else, such as another claim, prior art, or a specification. Claim charts must accompany the paper as an appendix. Claim charts are not a substitute for appropriate argument and explanation in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include claim charts where comparisons are required, and provide concomitant legal argument in the motion/paper itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions and replies content and admissions rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions and replies must comply with the content requirements for motions and must include a statement identifying material facts in dispute. Any material fact not specifically denied shall be considered admitted. All arguments for the relief requested in a motion must be made in the motion; a reply may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deny facts expressly when disputed; avoid raising new arguments in reply; uncontroverted facts may be deemed admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default filing schedules for motions and miscellaneous motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Default times: an opposition is due 30 days after service of the motion; a reply is due 30 days after service of the opposition; a responsive motion is due 30 days after service of the motion. For miscellaneous motions with no time provided: moving party must consult opposing party prior to filing; if opposing party plans to oppose, movant may not file without Board authorization. Oppositions to miscellaneous motions are due five business days after service; replies due three business days after service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult opposing parties for miscellaneous motions; obtain Board authorization to file if opposition is expected; adhere to default deadlines unless Board sets a different schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit filing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exhibit must be filed and served with the first paper in which it is cited except as the Board may otherwise order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not cite exhibits without filing and serving them with the citing paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument on papers: request timing and physical copies
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request an oral argument on an issue raised in a paper within five business days of the filing of the paper. The request must be filed as a separate paper and must specify the issues to be considered. If an oral argument is set for a panel, the movant must provide three working copies of the motion, the opposition, and the reply. Each party is responsible for providing three working copies of its exhibits relating to the motion. If granted, each party has a total of 20 minutes to present its arguments, including rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely request oral argument and prepare multiple working copies for the panel; plan arguments to fit 20-minute allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrative exhibits and transcription at oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrative exhibits must be served at least five business days before the oral argument and filed no later than the time of oral argument. The Board encourages transcription services at oral arguments; if used, notify the Board in advance and file the transcript promptly after the argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve demonstratives early and notify Board if transcription services will be used to ensure facilities are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on motions: discretion and interlocutory nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may take up motions in any order, may grant, deny, or dismiss any motion, and may defer action on an issue until later. A decision on motions without a judgment is not final for purposes of judicial review. A panel decision on an issue will govern further proceedings in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect interlocutory motion decisions and potential deferrals; panel rulings on issues generally bind further case proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing of motion decisions: timing and non-tolling rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rehearing of a decision on a motion must be filed within fourteen days of the decision. The filing of a request for rehearing does not toll times for taking action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act on overlapping deadlines because rehearing petitions do not pause other timing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration requirements and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may resort to binding arbitration to determine any issue in a contested case, conducted according to Title 9. The Office is not a party and the Board is not bound by arbitration; the Board will not authorize arbitration unless parties notify the Board in writing and an agreement is in writing specifying issues, naming an arbitrator or providing a selection date, and providing that the arbitrator’s award shall be binding and judgment may be entered by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbitration may be used by agreement of parties under Title 9 procedures; Board retains independent authority over patentability/jurisdiction/Office practice matters and will only authorize arbitration that meets formal written-agreement requirements.
